title: Adding Fractions with Unlike Denominators
short: Rename to like pieces, then add.
trouble: Children add the tops and the bottoms, so 1/2 + 1/3 becomes 2/5, which is less than 1/2.

blocks.html: You can add fractions with like denominators: $\frac{1}{5} + \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{5}$, because fifths add like apples. When the pieces are different sizes, first rename them with a common denominator.
To add fractions with unlike denominators, rename them with a common denominator, then add the numerators. The denominator stays the same, because it names the size of the pieces.

Adding counts pieces, and you can only count pieces of one size. $\frac{1}{3}$ is one big piece and $\frac{1}{4}$ is one smaller piece; together they are not “2 sevenths.” As twelfths they are 4 pieces and 3 pieces of the same size: 7 twelfths.

blocks.title: Unit fractions
steps: A common denominator of 2 and 3 is 6.

blocks.html: Adding the tops and the bottoms: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{5}$. A quick check shows it is wrong: $\frac{2}{5}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$, but adding $\frac{1}{3}$ to $\frac{1}{2}$ must give more than $\frac{1}{2}$.
